limits: True Web metadata receives a separate default five-minute active noninteractive budget spanning profile input, free-port work and certificate checking/verification. Explicit onNonInteractive Boolean callbacks pause consent/trust and resume the remaining budget; epochs reject stale timer callbacks.

Checks occur at runtime provider-reply, interaction-transition and runDotnet checkpoints; not every internal filesystem/network dispatch is elapsed-time-prechecked when a timer is undelivered. A normal prepareWebLaunch reply receives a monotonic post-check and permanently closes the budget before environment validation, later logging or handoff, preserving outcome/handoff safety. Original fatal errors retain priority unless an actual timeout/abort already selected another reason. Only the consent/trust interaction segment is paused; the existing per-call runProcess timeout continues during OS trust.

The existing Promise.all sibling-input-read policy stays unchanged: early rejection keeps siblings observed but does not promise actual drain of every filesystem request. Pure passive-input early rejection is narrow and does not establish OS I/O interruption or authorize abandoning write-capable providers. When both noncooperative input reads remain pending, the workflow/output/source gate stays held until the helper settles. Existing process/session/output ownership and actual drain semantics remain separate.

Generic runProcess and the owned file-app start helper remain baseline-equal. Existing save, SDK and handoff policies are separate; there is no hard OS/event-loop, whole-phase or actual-drain/disposal bound.
The one ordinary installed HTTP control is normal-flow regression only, without injected Web deadline expiry, held Web providers or HTTPS consent/trust interaction.

Replay validates retained EXE inputs against recorded original execution identities and boundaries without reading current cache contents or executing captured binaries. EXE-only retention is not a complete Python/runtime/stdlib/OS archive; historical collectors and records remain unchanged.
